title: Lattice torus coordinates, glued actions and Laurent base-change charts
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $L$ be an abelian group with a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ over $\mathbf Z$, $r\geq0$, and put $k[L]=\bigoplus_{l\in L}ke^l$ with $e^le^{l'}=e^{l+l'}$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}k[L]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The $k$-algebra isomorphism $k[L]\simeq k[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ sending $e^{\sum n_i b_i}$ to $\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$, with inverse $t_i\mapsto e^{b_i}$, identifies the group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] with comultiplication $e^l\mapsto e^l\otimes e^l$, counit $e^l\mapsto1$, and antipode $e^l\mapsto e^{-l}$ with the coordinate torus, whose multiplication, identity and inverse are coordinate multiplication, the tuple of ones and coordinate inversion.

If $N$ is a nonempty connected fine torsion-free monoscheme with a finite affine cover [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] and its generic stalk is identified with $L$, the chart coactions $k[P]\to k[L]\otimes_k k[P]$, $e^p\mapsto e^p\otimes e^p$, agree on overlaps and define an action of this group scheme on $k[N]$ satisfying the associativity and unit identities. For every $k$-scheme $Y$, the inverse image of every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ under $T\times_kY\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is canonically
$$\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_k k[L])\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(R[t_1,\ldots,t_r,u_1,\ldots,u_r]/(t_i u_i-1\mid1\leq i\leq r)\bigr),$$
where $c\otimes e^{\sum n_i b_i}\mapsto c\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$. These identifications commute with restriction to affine opens. The projection is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; if $Y$ is of finite type over $k$, so is $T\times_kY$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. In particular $T$ is of finite type over $k$. Rank zero and empty $Y$ are allowed.

proof.text: Use Mathlib MonoidAlgebra.domCongr k k b for the algebra coordinate map, and domCongrBialgEquiv for its comultiplication and counit compatibility. Its monomial formulas give the displayed formulas for the map and inverse. Induction over finite monomial sums and antipode_single proves antipode compatibility. Applying the contravariant hopfSpec functor to CommHopfAlgCat.isoMk of the inverse bialgebra equivalence gives the required group-scheme isomorphism, with exactly Spec.map of the inverse algebra map as its underlying map.

proof.text: Connectedness makes all connected-component classes equal. Each affine chart is therefore a component chart, and joint surjectivity of the realization colimit injections makes componentOpen the entire realization. Thus its open-subscheme inclusion is an isomorphism. The specification of existsUnique_torusAction gives its canonical chart formula. Construct the component-chart open cover directly from the union defining componentOpen. Pulling it back along the second projection and using the affine coaction scalar equation shows that torusAction is over k. Package this actual morphism as an Over morphism, and supply separately the unit and associativity diagrams from the two cited canonical-coaction lemmas. These are precisely the two proof fields of ModObj, whose smul is the prescribed torusAction.

proof.text: For every coefficient algebra R, compose MonoidAlgebra.scalarTensorEquiv k R with MonoidAlgebra.domCongr R R b. The scalarTensorEquiv_tmul and domCongr_single formulas send c tensor e^l to single (b l) c. Prove naturality by induction on tensor sums, followed by induction on monoid-algebra sums in the second factor; the single-monomial case is the fact that a k-algebra homomorphism commutes with the scalar map. This works for the zero coefficient ring as well.

proof.text: Let Q be the displayed polynomial quotient. The residue classes t_i and u_i multiply to one because their product minus one lies in the spanning relation ideal. They form explicit units v_i=(t_i,u_i). Send an integer vector n to the unit product of v_i raised to n_i, and extend its value to an R-algebra homomorphism from the group algebra to Q using MonoidAlgebra.lift. In the other direction evaluate the polynomial variables at positive and negative standard monomials; every relation evaluates to zero, so Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ descends this map. The composite on Q fixes its polynomial generators. For the group-algebra composite, decompose every vector as the sum of its integer multiples of standard vectors; the unit homomorphism preserves this product and all integer powers, hence fixes every monomial. Algebra-hom extensionality gives both inverse identities. AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom packages the equivalence, whose evaluation formulas on both kinds of generators are the original polynomial evaluations. Empty products prove the rank-zero case, and no nontriviality hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Use pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso to paste the pullback along j with the torus projection. The Over equation j.left followed by Y.hom equals the scalar spectrum map identifies its base map with Spec R to Spec k. Apply pullback.congrHom, then pullbackSymmetry, then pullbackSpecIso k R k[L]. The two projection formulas follow by pullback extensionality, the pasting and symmetry projection equations, and pullbackSpecIso_hom_fst and pullbackSpecIso_hom_snd. This is valid for every j over the base, in particular every affine open chart.

proof.text: The coordinate group of integer vectors is finitely generated, and transfer along b gives Group.FG L. Mathlib MonoidAlgebra.finiteType_of_fg therefore gives Algebra.FiniteType k k[L]. Since k is a field it is Noetherian, and Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType makes this algebra finitely presented. LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff gives the local finite presentation of its spectrum map. Stability under arbitrary base change gives the asserted projection property for every Y. Local finite type follows from local finite presentation; affine spectrum maps are quasi-compact. Base change preserves both properties, and composition with the finite-type structure map of Y proves the conjunction for the composite. This argument handles rank zero and empty Y without additional cases.

lean.statement: theorem latticeTorus_coordinates (k : Type u) [Field k] (L : Type u) [CommGroup L] (r : ℕ) (b : L ≃* Multiplicative (Fin r → ℤ)) : ∃ e : MonoidAlgebra k L ≃ₐ[k] MonoidAlgebra k (Multiplicative (Fin r → ℤ)), (∀ l : L, e (MonoidAlgebra.single l 1) = MonoidAlgebra.single (b l) 1) ∧ (∀ n : Multiplicative (Fin r → ℤ), e.symm (MonoidAlgebra.single n 1) = MonoidAlgebra.single (b.symm n) 1) ∧ (∀ x : MonoidAlgebra k L, (Algebra.TensorProduct.map e.toAlgHom e.toAlgHom) (Coalgebra.comul x) = Coalgebra.comul (e x)) ∧ (∀ x : MonoidAlgebra k L, Coalgebra.counit (e x) = (Coalgebra.counit x : k)) ∧ (∀ x : MonoidAlgebra k L, e (HopfAlgebra.antipode k x) = HopfAlgebra.antipode k (e x)) ∧ ∃ i : Grp.mk ((Spec (.of (MonoidAlgebra k L))).asOver (Spec (.of k))) ≅ Grp.mk ((Spec (.of (MonoidAlgebra k (Multiplicative (Fin r → ℤ))))).asOver (Spec (.of k))), i.hom.hom.hom.left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom e.symm.toRingHom)
